1. Spoofing of Destination Data Store Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Event store may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being written to the attacker's target instead of Event store. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination data store.
Justification:The event store is the event table in the Keycloak database, written only when Save events is on. Keycloak reaches its database over the configured JDBC connection with a dedicated database account. Restrict that account to the Keycloak schema, require TLS with certificate validation on the JDBC URL (Keycloak does not enforce it), and keep the database on a segment only Keycloak nodes can reach.

2. Potential SQL Injection Vulnerability for Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. Any procedure that constructs SQL statements should be reviewed for injection vulnerabilities because SQL Server will execute all syntactically valid queries that it receives. Even parameterized data can be manipulated by a skilled and determined attacker.
Justification:Keycloak writes events through JPA/Hibernate with bound parameters, so request details are stored as values, not SQL.

3. Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Manage user account (register, reset password, update) or Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Does Manage user account (register, reset password, update) or Event store take explicit steps to control resource consumption? Resource consumption attacks can be hard to deal with, and there are times that it makes sense to let the OS do the job. Be careful that your resource requests don't deadlock, and that they do timeout.
Justification:Saved events have a configurable expiration, which bounds table growth; the SIEM keeps the long-term copy.

Interaction: Account pages and responses

4. Spoofing of the End user (browser) External Destination Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:End user (browser) may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being sent to the attacker's target instead of End user (browser). Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:Pages are returned on the user&#39;s own TLS connection, and reset links are only emailed to the address on the account.

5. External Entity End user (browser) Potentially Denies Receiving Data  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:End user (browser) claims that it did not receive data from a process on the other side of the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:REGISTER, UPDATE_PASSWORD, RESET_PASSWORD, SEND_RESET_PASSWORD and UPDATE_PROFILE events record these actions. Save events is off by default and only error events reach the server log, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:The user reloads or requests a new link; unused action tokens expire.

9. Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Administer realm (Admin console) or Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service

11. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Administer realm (Admin console)' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:The Admin Console is a React app that escapes rendered values, and the Admin REST API returns JSON, not HTML. Stored values that reach login pages are escaped by FreeMarker&#39;s HTML auto-escaping. Stay on patched releases.

12. Persistent Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Administer realm (Admin console)' could be a subject to a persistent cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize data store 'Keycloak database' inputs and output.
Justification:Stored realm settings such as display names are escaped when shown. The Admin Console is a React app that escapes rendered values, and the Admin REST API returns JSON, not HTML. Stored values that reach login pages are escaped by FreeMarker&#39;s HTML auto-escaping. Stay on patched releases.

13. Weak Access Control for a Resource  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Improper data protection of Keycloak database can allow an attacker to read information not intended for disclosure. Review authorization settings.
Justification:Admin REST API responses drop user credentials and mask client secrets, IdP client secrets and SMTP passwords (StripSecretsUtils). Since 26.8.0, admins who only hold view-clients no longer receive client secrets. Grant admin roles by need.

Interaction: Admin requests

14. Spoofing the Realm admin (browser) External Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Realm admin (browser) may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Administer realm (Admin console). Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:Gap by default: the browser flow only asks for OTP if the admin already set it up, brute force detection is off for new realms, and the bootstrap admin is password-only. Our configuration requires OTP for every master-realm admin, turns on brute force detection, and limits /admin/ to the admin network at the reverse proxy.

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Administer realm (Admin console)' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.

16. Potential Data Repudiation by Administer realm (Admin console)  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Administer realm (Admin console) claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:Admin events record the operation, resource path and admin, but Save admin events is off for new realms and successful events only reach the server log at debug level. Our configuration turns admin events on and forwards them to the SIEM. The reset-password admin event has no representation, so it shows which user was reset but not the new value.

17. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Administer realm (Admin console)  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Administer realm (Admin console) crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:Keycloak has no per-client or per-IP rate limiting. Set http-max-queued-requests (no limit by default) so the server sheds load, rate-limit at the reverse proxy, and run at least two nodes. The Admin Console and Admin REST API should only be reachable from the admin network.

18. Data Flow Admin requests Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:Each Admin REST call is a single request. A call that does not complete changes nothing, and the admin retries.

19. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Administer realm (Admin console) may be able to impersonate the context of Realm admin (browser) in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:Gap: reset-password rights fall back to manage on the target user, and canManage does not look at the target&#39;s roles. A manage-users admin can reset a realm-admin&#39;s password, remove their OTP and sign in as them. Impersonation checks for higher privileges, but password reset doesn&#39;t. Limit who holds manage-users and review resets through admin events.

20. Administer realm (Admin console) May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Realm admin (browser) may be able to remotely execute code for Administer realm (Admin console).
Justification:The process parses requests and directory responses with standard libraries and never evaluates input as code. Keep Keycloak and its Java runtime patched and run it as an unprivileged user. Admins cannot upload scripts through the Admin Console; custom providers must be deployed as JARs on the server.

21. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Administer realm (Admin console)  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Administer realm (Admin console) in order to change the flow of program execution within Administer realm (Admin console) to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:Every Admin REST endpoint checks the caller&#39;s permissions on the server (requireManage, requireResetPassword and similar). Keycloak 26.8.1 fixed two paths that skipped the reset-password check (CVE-2026-97177, CVE-2026-94001), so run 26.8.1 or later.

22. Cross Site Request Forgery  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Cross-site request forgery (CSRF or XSRF) is a type of attack in which an attacker forces a user's browser to make a forged request to a vulnerable site by exploiting an existing trust relationship between the browser and the vulnerable web site. In a simple scenario, a user is logged in to web site A using a cookie as a credential. The other browses to web site B. Web site B returns a page with a hidden form that posts to web site A. Since the browser will carry the user's cookie to web site A, web site B now can take any action on web site A, for example, adding an admin to an account. The attack can be used to exploit any requests that the browser automatically authenticates, e.g. by session cookie, integrated authentication, IP whitelisting. The attack can be carried out in many ways such as by luring the victim to a site under control of the attacker, getting the user to click a link in a phishing email, or hacking a reputable web site that the victim will visit. The issue can only be resolved on the server side by requiring that all authenticated state-changing requests include an additional piece of secret payload (canary or CSRF token) which is known only to the legitimate web site and the browser and which is protected in transit through SSL/TLS. See the Forgery Protection property on the flow stencil for a list of mitigations.
Justification:The Admin REST API authenticates with a bearer token in the Authorization header, not a cookie, so a forged cross-site request carries no credentials.

Interaction: Admin responses

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Does Authenticate user or Event store take explicit steps to control resource consumption? Resource consumption attacks can be hard to deal with, and there are times that it makes sense to let the OS do the job. Be careful that your resource requests don't deadlock, and that they do timeout.

29. Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Authenticate user or Session store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Does Authenticate user or Session store take explicit steps to control resource consumption? Resource consumption attacks can be hard to deal with, and there are times that it makes sense to let the OS do the job. Be careful that your resource requests don't deadlock, and that they do timeout.
Justification:Codes are single-use and expire with the client login timeout, and the number of authentication sessions per browser session is capped. Cache sizing is a deployment setting.

30. Spoofing of Destination Data Store Session store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Session store may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being written to the attacker's target instead of Session store. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination data store.
Justification:The session store is Keycloak&#39;s embedded Infinispan cache, persisted to the Keycloak database. Cluster traffic between nodes is TLS-encrypted by default, and nodes need the cluster certificate stored in the database to join.

Interaction: Authorization request

31. Spoofing the End user (browser) External Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:End user (browser) may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Authenticate user. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:The browser does not identify anyone by itself; Authenticate user establishes the user&#39;s identity through the login flow (Interaction 1). For this flow the parameters that matter are client_id and redirect_uri: Keycloak checks redirect_uri against the client&#39;s registered values, and PKCE (S256, required through the pkce-enforcer client policy) binds the code to whoever started the flow.

32. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Authenticate user' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Login and broker pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat). Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

33. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Authenticate user may be able to impersonate the context of End user (browser) in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:The authorization request grants nothing until the user authenticates. Requested scopes are limited to the client scopes assigned to the client, and Full Scope Allowed is turned off (full-scope-disabled client policy) so tokens carry only the client&#39;s role scope mappings.

34. Cross Site Request Forgery  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Cross-site request forgery (CSRF or XSRF) is a type of attack in which an attacker forces a user's browser to make a forged request to a vulnerable site by exploiting an existing trust relationship between the browser and the vulnerable web site. In a simple scenario, a user is logged in to web site A using a cookie as a credential. The other browses to web site B. Web site B returns a page with a hidden form that posts to web site A. Since the browser will carry the user's cookie to web site A, web site B now can take any action on web site A, for example, adding an admin to an account. The attack can be used to exploit any requests that the browser automatically authenticates, e.g. by session cookie, integrated authentication, IP whitelisting. The attack can be carried out in many ways such as by luring the victim to a site under control of the attacker, getting the user to click a link in a phishing email, or hacking a reputable web site that the victim will visit. The issue can only be resolved on the server side by requiring that all authenticated state-changing requests include an additional piece of secret payload (canary or CSRF token) which is known only to the legitimate web site and the browser and which is protected in transit through SSL/TLS. See the Forgery Protection property on the flow stencil for a list of mitigations.
Justification:Login form posts must carry the authentication session&#39;s session_code and tab_id along with the session cookie, so a forged cross-site post does not match. The OIDC state parameter protects the client side and must be checked by the client.

35. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Authenticate user  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Authenticate user in order to change the flow of program execution within Authenticate user to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:Authentication flows are server-side and bound to the authentication session (session_code, execution, tab_id). A request that skips or replays a step is rejected and the flow restarts.

36. Authenticate user May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:End user (browser) may be able to remotely execute code for Authenticate user.
Justification:The process parses parameters and tokens with standard libraries and never evaluates input as code. Keep Keycloak and its Java runtime patched and run it as an unprivileged user.

37. Data Flow Authorization request Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:Production mode refuses to start without HTTPS, which protects integrity. If this flow is interrupted, no code, token, or session is issued, so the login fails closed and the user starts over.

38. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Authenticate user  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Authenticate user crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:Brute-force detection limits repeated login failures (Interaction 1). Keycloak has no per-client or per-IP rate limiting. Set http-max-queued-requests (no limit by default) so the server sheds load, and rate-limit by client and source IP at the reverse proxy. Run at least two nodes.

39. Potential Data Repudiation by Authenticate user  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Authenticate user claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:Keycloak records LOGIN, LOGIN_ERROR and CODE_TO_TOKEN events with client_id, IP and session. Save events is off by default and only error events reach the server log, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

Interaction: Authorization response

40. Data Flow Authorization response Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:An undelivered code is never redeemed and expires with the client login timeout, 60 seconds by default; we set it under 10 seconds as Keycloak&#39;s threat docs advise. The user restarts login.

41. External Entity End user (browser) Potentially Denies Receiving Data  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:End user (browser) claims that it did not receive data from a process on the other side of the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:The LOGIN event records the code being issued, and a matching CODE_TO_TOKEN event (or its absence) shows whether the client redeemed it. Save events is off by default and only error events reach the server log, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

42. Spoofing of the End user (browser) External Destination Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:End user (browser) may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being sent to the attacker's target instead of End user (browser). Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:This is the redirect URI manipulation threat. Register exact redirect URIs and enable the secure-redirect-uris-enforcer client policy (off by default) so wildcard and loopback registrations are rejected; a trailing * is otherwise honored as a prefix match. For confidential clients, the client secret stops an attacker from redeeming a misdelivered code.

Interaction: Bind result

43. Spoofing the Synchronize federated users Process  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Synchronize federated users may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to information disclosure by Active Directory. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination process.
Justification:AD answers on the connection Keycloak opened, so a substituted process cannot receive the result. With TLS required (ldaps:// or StartTLS) the connection is encrypted and AD&#39;s certificate is checked.

44. Spoofing the Active Directory External Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Active Directory may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Synchronize federated users. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:Use an ldaps:// URL or turn on StartTLS. Keycloak accepts a plaintext ldap:// URL without a warning, so our configuration requires TLS. With TLS on, Keycloak checks AD&#39;s certificate against its truststore and always uses strict hostname verification (LDAPUtil).

45. Potential Lack of Input Validation for Synchronize federated users  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:Data flowing across Bind result may be tampered with by an attacker. This may lead to a denial of service attack against Synchronize federated users or an elevation of privilege attack against Synchronize federated users or an information disclosure by Synchronize federated users. Failure to verify that input is as expected is a root cause of a very large number of exploitable issues. Consider all paths and the way they handle data. Verify that all input is verified for correctness using an approved list input validation approach.
Justification:The bind result is an LDAP result code read through the standard JNDI provider. Anything other than success is treated as a failed login.

46. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Not Applicable]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Synchronize federated users' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:The bind result is a status code that is never rendered in a page, so cross-site scripting does not apply to this flow.

47. Potential Data Repudiation by Synchronize federated users  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Synchronize federated users claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:AD&#39;s own security log records the bind or query on its side. On the Keycloak side, LOGIN and LOGIN_ERROR events record the outcome when Save events is on; it is off by default, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

48. Data Flow Sniffing  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Data flowing across Bind result may be sniffed by an attacker. Depending on what type of data an attacker can read, it may be used to attack other parts of the system or simply be a disclosure of information leading to compliance violations. Consider encrypting the data flow.
Justification:Use an ldaps:// URL or turn on StartTLS. Keycloak accepts a plaintext ldap:// URL without a warning, so our configuration requires TLS. With TLS on, Keycloak checks AD&#39;s certificate against its truststore and always uses strict hostname verification (LDAPUtil). Without TLS, user passwords cross the network in clear text.

49. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Synchronize federated users  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Synchronize federated users crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:The connection timeout defaults to 5 seconds, but the read timeout has no default, so a domain controller that accepts the connection and then stops answering can hold login requests. Set a read timeout and list more than one domain controller (space-separated URLs give failover).

50. Data Flow Bind result Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:An interrupted bind is treated as a failed login, so nothing is granted and the user tries again. The connection timeout defaults to 5 seconds, but the read timeout has no default, so a domain controller that accepts the connection and then stops answering can hold login requests. Set a read timeout and list more than one domain controller (space-separated URLs give failover).

51. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Synchronize federated users may be able to impersonate the context of Active Directory in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:Keycloak only accepts a successful bind for the DN it looked up for that username, so one user&#39;s password cannot sign in another account. Brute force detection, which our configuration turns on, limits guessing.

52. Synchronize federated users May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Active Directory may be able to remotely execute code for Synchronize federated users.
Justification:The process parses requests and directory responses with standard libraries and never evaluates input as code. Keep Keycloak and its Java runtime patched and run it as an unprivileged user.

53. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Synchronize federated users  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Synchronize federated users in order to change the flow of program execution within Synchronize federated users to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:The LDAP provider only treats a successful bind for the expected DN as a valid login; any error ends the login.

Interaction: Broker login events

54. Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Broker external login or Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Does Broker external login or Event store take explicit steps to control resource consumption? Resource consumption attacks can be hard to deal with, and there are times that it makes sense to let the OS do the job. Be careful that your resource requests don't deadlock, and that they do timeout.
Justification:Saved events have a configurable expiration, which bounds table growth; the SIEM keeps the long-term copy.

55. Potential SQL Injection Vulnerability for Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. Any procedure that constructs SQL statements should be reviewed for injection vulnerabilities because SQL Server will execute all syntactically valid queries that it receives. Even parameterized data can be manipulated by a skilled and determined attacker.
Justification:Keycloak writes events through JPA/Hibernate with bound parameters, so request details are stored as values, not SQL.

56. Spoofing of Destination Data Store Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Event store may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being written to the attacker's target instead of Event store. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination data store.
Justification:The event store is the event table in the Keycloak database, written only when Save events is on. Keycloak reaches its database over the configured JDBC connection with a dedicated database account. Restrict that account to the Keycloak schema, require TLS with certificate validation on the JDBC URL (Keycloak does not enforce it), and keep the database on a segment only Keycloak nodes can reach.

Interaction: Broker login request

57. Spoofing the End user (browser) External Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:End user (browser) may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Broker external login. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:The broker login request only starts a redirect to the partner. It must carry the current authentication session reference (session_code, client_id, tab_id) and grants nothing by itself; the user&#39;s identity comes from the partner&#39;s signed assertion (SAML response).

58. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Broker external login' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Login and broker pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat). Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

59. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Broker external login may be able to impersonate the context of End user (browser) in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:Broker external login acts only within the browser&#39;s authentication session. Account Linking Only and disabled-client checks run on every brokered login (CVE-2026-16442 fix).

60. Potential Data Repudiation by Broker external login  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Broker external login claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:IDENTITY_PROVIDER_LOGIN and its error events record brokered logins. Save events is off by default and only error events reach the server log, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

61. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Broker external login  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Broker external login crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:Keycloak has no per-client or per-IP rate limiting. Set http-max-queued-requests (no limit by default) so the server sheds load, and rate-limit by client and source IP at the reverse proxy. Run at least two nodes.

62. Data Flow Broker login request Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:If this flow is interrupted, no code, token, or session is issued, so the login fails closed and the user starts over.

63. Broker external login May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:End user (browser) may be able to remotely execute code for Broker external login.
Justification:The process parses parameters and tokens with standard libraries and never evaluates input as code. Keep Keycloak and its Java runtime patched and run it as an unprivileged user.

64. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Broker external login  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Broker external login in order to change the flow of program execution within Broker external login to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:The broker endpoint validates the authentication session and the provider alias, and rejects disabled providers and link-only providers for login.

65. Cross Site Request Forgery  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Cross-site request forgery (CSRF or XSRF) is a type of attack in which an attacker forces a user's browser to make a forged request to a vulnerable site by exploiting an existing trust relationship between the browser and the vulnerable web site. In a simple scenario, a user is logged in to web site A using a cookie as a credential. The other browses to web site B. Web site B returns a page with a hidden form that posts to web site A. Since the browser will carry the user's cookie to web site A, web site B now can take any action on web site A, for example, adding an admin to an account. The attack can be used to exploit any requests that the browser automatically authenticates, e.g. by session cookie, integrated authentication, IP whitelisting. The attack can be carried out in many ways such as by luring the victim to a site under control of the attacker, getting the user to click a link in a phishing email, or hacking a reputable web site that the victim will visit. The issue can only be resolved on the server side by requiring that all authenticated state-changing requests include an additional piece of secret payload (canary or CSRF token) which is known only to the legitimate web site and the browser and which is protected in transit through SSL/TLS. See the Forgery Protection property on the flow stencil for a list of mitigations.
Justification:The request must carry the current authentication session&#39;s session_code and tab_id with the session cookie, so a forged cross-site request is rejected.

Interaction: Brokered identity context

66. Broker external login Process Memory Tampered  [State: Not Applicable]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:If Broker external login is given access to memory, such as shared memory or pointers, or is given the ability to control what Authenticate user executes (for example, passing back a function pointer.), then Broker external login can tamper with Authenticate user. Consider if the function could work with less access to memory, such as passing data rather than pointers. Copy in data provided, and then validate it.
Justification:Broker external login and Authenticate user are parts of the same Keycloak server process; the brokered identity is passed as an in-memory object, not across a trust boundary or shared memory.

Category:Tampering

Justification:Brokered attributes shown on the review-profile page are escaped. Login and broker pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat). Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

68. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Authenticate user may be able to impersonate the context of Broker external login in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:Authenticate user runs the first broker login flow before linking or creating an account. The default flow requires email verification or re-authentication before linking (SR-4.2); an auto-link flow must not be used for the partner.

Resource consumption attacks can be hard to deal with, and there are times that it makes sense to let the OS do the job. Be careful that your resource requests don't deadlock, and that they do timeout.
Justification:Each brokered login creates at most one user and one identity link. Watch for unusual growth in users linked to the partner provider.

72. Weak Access Control for a Resource  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Improper data protection of Keycloak database can allow an attacker to read information not intended for disclosure. Review authorization settings.
Justification:Largest gap in Interaction 3. The database holds client secrets as entered (compared directly, not hashed) unless they are vault references, plus each realm&#39;s generated signing keys, including the HMAC key that signs refresh tokens. Read access to the database is enough to forge tokens. Mitigations: vault references for client secrets, the java-keystore key provider instead of generated keys, restricted and audited database access, and encryption at rest.
