Since the browser will carry the user's cookie to web site A, web site B now can take any action on web site A, for example, adding an admin to an account. The attack can be used to exploit any requests that the browser automatically authenticates, e.g. by session cookie, integrated authentication, IP whitelisting. The attack can be carried out in many ways such as by luring the victim to a site under control of the attacker, getting the user to click a link in a phishing email, or hacking a reputable web site that the victim will visit. The issue can only be resolved on the server side by requiring that all authenticated state-changing requests include an additional piece of secret payload (canary or CSRF token) which is known only to the legitimate web site and the browser and which is protected in transit through SSL/TLS. See the Forgery Protection property on the flow stencil for a list of mitigations.
Justification:Keycloak authentication forms use session-bound parameters such as session_code and tab_id. Verify that OTP submission requires valid authentication-session context and rejects forged cross-site requests.

111. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Authenticate user  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Authenticate user in order to change the flow of program execution within Authenticate user to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:Authentication steps are managed server-side and associated with an authentication session. Verify that replayed, skipped, or manipulated OTP submissions cannot bypass the required authentication flow, including custom extensions.

112. Authenticate user May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:End user (browser) may be able to remotely execute code for Authenticate user.
Justification:OTP input is processed by Keycloak authentication components. Review input handling, custom authenticators, deployed Keycloak and Java patch levels, and security testing before concluding that remote code execution is mitigated.

113. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Authenticate user may be able to impersonate the context of End user (browser) in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:The OTP response should be accepted only for the correct user and active authentication session. Verify OTP freshness, one-time use, session binding, and required authentication steps to assess impersonation risk.

114. Data Flow OTP response (code) Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:An attacker or network failure could interrupt the OTP response, preventing authentication from completing. Verify TLS protection, timeout handling, safe retry behavior, and availability controls. This remains an availability risk.

115. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Authenticate user  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Authenticate user crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:Brute-force protection, reverse-proxy rate limiting, request queue limits, and multiple application nodes can reduce availability risks. Verify that these protections are enabled and tested for OTP submissions.

116. Potential Data Repudiation by Authenticate user  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Authenticate user claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:Keycloak supports authentication events and error logging, but event persistence and SIEM forwarding depend on configuration. Verify that OTP successes and failures are logged and retained.

117. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Authenticate user' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Keycloak login pages use FreeMarker templates with HTML auto-escaping. However, custom themes and the deployed patch level must be reviewed to confirm that OTP input cannot introduce cross-site scripting.

118. Spoofing the End user (browser) External Entity  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:End user (browser) may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Authenticate user. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:Keycloak verifies the user&#39;s identity through its authentication flow rather than trusting the browser. The OTP response must be associated with the correct authentication session. Verify session binding and OTP validation before confirming mitigation.

Interaction: Registration, password reset and account requests

119. Spoofing the End user (browser) External Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:End user (browser) may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Manage user account (register, reset password, update). Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:Account changes require an authenticated session, and a password reset requires the single-use action token emailed to the account&#39;s address. Self-registration and Forgot password are off unless enabled. Brute force detection, which our configuration turns on, limits guessing.

120. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Manage user account (register, reset password, update)' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Login and account pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat), and the Account and Admin Consoles are React apps that escape rendered values. Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

121. Potential Data Repudiation by Manage user account (register, reset password, update)  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Manage user account (register, reset password, update) claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:REGISTER, UPDATE_PASSWORD, RESET_PASSWORD, SEND_RESET_PASSWORD and UPDATE_PROFILE events record these actions. Save events is off by default and only error events reach the server log, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

122. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Manage user account (register, reset password, update)  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Manage user account (register, reset password, update) crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:Keycloak has no per-client or per-IP rate limiting. Set http-max-queued-requests (no limit by default) so the server sheds load, rate-limit at the reverse proxy, and run at least two nodes. Registration and reset requests can trigger emails, so rate-limit those endpoints at the proxy.

123. Data Flow Registration, password reset and account requests Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:Nothing is changed until the request completes, so an interrupted request leaves the account as it was and the user retries. Unused action tokens expire.

124. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Manage user account (register, reset password, update) may be able to impersonate the context of End user (browser) in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:Resetting a password requires the single-use action token sent to the account&#39;s email address, and the token expires. An attacker would need access to that mailbox.

125. Manage user account (register, reset password, update) May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:End user (browser) may be able to remotely execute code for Manage user account (register, reset password, update).
Justification:The process parses requests and directory responses with standard libraries and never evaluates input as code. Keep Keycloak and its Java runtime patched and run it as an unprivileged user.

126. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Manage user account (register, reset password, update)  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Manage user account (register, reset password, update) in order to change the flow of program execution within Manage user account (register, reset password, update) to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:Required actions and the reset-credentials flow are server-side flows bound to the authentication session (session_code, execution, tab_id). A request that skips or replays a step is rejected.

127. Cross Site Request Forgery  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Cross-site request forgery (CSRF or XSRF) is a type of attack in which an attacker forces a user's browser to make a forged request to a vulnerable site by exploiting an existing trust relationship between the browser and the vulnerable web site. In a simple scenario, a user is logged in to web site A using a cookie as a credential. The other browses to web site B. Web site B returns a page with a hidden form that posts to web site A. Since the browser will carry the user's cookie to web site A, web site B now can take any action on web site A, for example, adding an admin to an account. The attack can be used to exploit any requests that the browser automatically authenticates, e.g. by session cookie, integrated authentication, IP whitelisting. The attack can be carried out in many ways such as by luring the victim to a site under control of the attacker, getting the user to click a link in a phishing email, or hacking a reputable web site that the victim will visit. The issue can only be resolved on the server side by requiring that all authenticated state-changing requests include an additional piece of secret payload (canary or CSRF token) which is known only to the legitimate web site and the browser and which is protected in transit through SSL/TLS. See the Forgery Protection property on the flow stencil for a list of mitigations.
Justification:Login-action form posts must carry the authentication session&#39;s session_code and tab_id along with the session cookie, so a forged cross-site post does not match. The Account Console calls the Account REST API with a bearer token in the Authorization header, not a cookie.

Interaction: SAML authentication request

128. Weakness in SSO Authorization  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Common SSO implementations such as OAUTH2 and OAUTH Wrap are vulnerable to MitM attacks.
Justification:SAML messages pass through the browser over HTTPS. Want AuthnRequests Signed lets the partner verify Keycloak&#39;s request, and Validate Signature plus Identity Provider Entity ID make Keycloak verify the response. The request ID is stored in the authentication session and must come back as InResponseTo.

129. Spoofing of the Partner identity provider External Destination Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Partner identity provider may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being sent to the attacker's target instead of Partner identity provider. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:The partner&#39;s single sign-on URL is fixed in the provider configuration (or imported from partner metadata over TLS), so the browser is only sent there.

130. External Entity Partner identity provider Potentially Denies Receiving Data  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Partner identity provider claims that it did not receive data from a process on the other side of the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:Keycloak keeps the outgoing request ID in the authentication session, and the partner&#39;s response must reference it. The partner&#39;s own logs cover its side.

131. Data Flow SAML authentication request Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:If the partner is unreachable, brokered login fails and no session is created; employees still log in directly (Interaction 1).

Interaction: SAML response

132. Spoofing the Partner identity provider External Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Partner identity provider may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Broker external login. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:Turn on Validate Signature with the partner&#39;s signing certificate pinned (or loaded from its metadata URL over TLS) and set Identity Provider Entity ID. Without them Keycloak accepts unsigned responses and skips the Issuer check, and Want Assertions Signed alone only checks that a signature is present. SP-initiated responses are bound to the request ID; leave the IDP-Initiated SSO URL name unset on partner-facing clients so unsolicited responses are refused.

133. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Broker external login' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Assertion attribute values shown on the first broker login review-profile page are escaped. Login and broker pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat). Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

134. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Broker external login may be able to impersonate the context of Partner identity provider in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:The partner can assert group values that mappers turn into roles. Our design maps the partner only to a contractor role and uses Force sync mode so roles are re-checked each login, and 26.8.0 (CVE-2026-12388) blocks admin roles through mappers by default. Gap: anyone with manage-identity-providers can still create a mapper that grants non-admin business roles such as finance or payroll.

135. Potential Data Repudiation by Broker external login  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Broker external login claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:With Save events on, IDENTITY_PROVIDER_LOGIN, IDENTITY_PROVIDER_FIRST_LOGIN and FEDERATED_IDENTITY_LINK record brokered logins, and Store Tokens keeps the latest assertion. Gap: both are off by default, and role grants made by mappers emit no event, so a grant cannot be traced back to the assertion that caused it.

136. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Broker external login  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Broker external login crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:The SAML parser rejects DOCTYPE declarations and external entities (DocumentUtil, StaxParserUtil), which blocks entity-expansion attacks. Cap request size and rate at the reverse proxy and set http-max-queued-requests.

137. Data Flow SAML response Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:If the response never arrives, the authentication session expires and the user restarts login; nothing is created.

138. Broker external login May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Partner identity provider may be able to remotely execute code for Broker external login.
Justification:XML parsing is hardened as above, and signatures are verified on the element Keycloak actually reads. The process parses parameters and tokens with standard libraries and never evaluates input as code. Keep Keycloak and its Java runtime patched and run it as an unprivileged user.

139. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Broker external login  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Broker external login in order to change the flow of program execution within Broker external login to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:IdP-initiated logins only work for clients with an IDP-Initiated SSO URL name, and Account Linking Only and disabled-client checks run on every entry point (CVE-2026-16442 fix). The default first broker login flow requires email verification or re-authentication before linking an existing account; Trust Email stays off for the partner.

Interaction: Token events

140. Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Issue tokens or Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Does Issue tokens or Event store take explicit steps to control resource consumption? Resource consumption attacks can be hard to deal with, and there are times that it makes sense to let the OS do the job. Be careful that your resource requests don't deadlock, and that they do timeout.
Justification:Saved events have a configurable expiration, which bounds table growth; the SIEM keeps the long-term copy.

141. Potential SQL Injection Vulnerability for Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. Any procedure that constructs SQL statements should be reviewed for injection vulnerabilities because SQL Server will execute all syntactically valid queries that it receives. Even parameterized data can be manipulated by a skilled and determined attacker.
Justification:Keycloak writes events through JPA/Hibernate with bound parameters, so request details are stored as values, not SQL.

142. Spoofing of Destination Data Store Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Event store may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being written to the attacker's target instead of Event store. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination data store.
Justification:The event store is the event table in the Keycloak database, written only when Save events is on. Keycloak reaches its database over the configured JDBC connection with a dedicated database account. Restrict that account to the Keycloak schema, require TLS with certificate validation on the JDBC URL (Keycloak does not enforce it), and keep the database on a segment only Keycloak nodes can reach.

Interaction: Token request

143. Spoofing the Client application External Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Client application may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Issue tokens. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:Confidential clients authenticate at the token endpoint (client secret by default; we require signed JWT or mTLS). Public clients cannot authenticate, so PKCE S256 is required for them through the pkce-enforcer client policy (off by default), and redirect_uri must match the one used in the authorization request.

144. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Not Applicable]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Issue tokens' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Issue tokens is a back-channel JSON endpoint and renders no HTML, so cross-site scripting does not apply to this flow.

145. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Issue tokens may be able to impersonate the context of Client application in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:A stolen refresh token lets an attacker act as the client. Mitigations: Revoke Refresh Token with Refresh Token Max Reuse 0 (realm-wide, off by default), DPoP binding for public clients, and short access tokens. Gap: Keycloak rejects a reused refresh token as stale but does not revoke the still-active token chain (SR-3.6), so a thief who refreshes first keeps access until the session ends.

146. Potential Data Repudiation by Issue tokens  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Issue tokens claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:Keycloak records CODE_TO_TOKEN, REFRESH_TOKEN and their error events with client_id and IP. Save events is off by default and only error events reach the server log, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

147. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Issue tokens  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Issue tokens crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:Keycloak has no per-client or per-IP rate limiting. Set http-max-queued-requests (no limit by default) so the server sheds load, and rate-limit by client and source IP at the reverse proxy. Run at least two nodes.

148. Data Flow Token request Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:TLS protects integrity. A code is removed from the store when it is redeemed, so an interrupted redemption means the user logs in again; refresh requests can simply be retried.

149. Issue tokens May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Client application may be able to remotely execute code for Issue tokens.
Justification:The process parses parameters and tokens with standard libraries and never evaluates input as code. Keep Keycloak and its Java runtime patched and run it as an unprivileged user.

150. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Issue tokens  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Issue tokens in order to change the flow of program execution within Issue tokens to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:Each grant type has its own handler. The authorization code grant checks that the code is valid and unused, belongs to the calling client, matches redirect_uri, and passes PKCE before issuing tokens (AuthorizationCodeGrantType).

Interaction: Token response

151. Spoofing of the Client application External Destination Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Client application may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being sent to the attacker's target instead of Client application. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:Tokens go back on the TLS connection the client opened, so only the party that authenticated or presented the PKCE verifier receives them. Turning off Full Scope Allowed and setting audiences limits what a misdirected token can do.

152. External Entity Client application Potentially Denies Receiving Data  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Client application claims that it did not receive data from a process on the other side of the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:CODE_TO_TOKEN and REFRESH_TOKEN events record issuance to the client. Save events is off by default and only error events reach the server log, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

153. Data Flow Token response Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:The client retries with a refresh token or restarts login; the consumed code cannot be reused.

Interaction: User account changes

154. Spoofing of Destination Data Store Keycloak database  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Keycloak database may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being written to the attacker's target instead of Keycloak database. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination data store.
Justification:Keycloak reaches its database over the configured JDBC connection with a dedicated database account. Restrict that account to the Keycloak schema, require TLS with certificate validation on the JDBC URL (Keycloak does not enforce it), and keep the database on a segment only Keycloak nodes can reach.

155. Potential SQL Injection Vulnerability for Keycloak database  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. Any procedure that constructs SQL statements should be reviewed for injection vulnerabilities because SQL Server will execute all syntactically valid queries that it receives. Even parameterized data can be manipulated by a skilled and determined attacker.
Justification:Keycloak writes through JPA/Hibernate with bound parameters, so request and directory values are stored as data, not SQL.

156. Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Manage user account (register, reset password, update) or Keycloak database  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Does Manage user account (register, reset password, update) or Keycloak database take explicit steps to control resource consumption? Resource consumption attacks can be hard to deal with, and there are times that it makes sense to let the OS do the job. Be careful that your resource requests don't deadlock, and that they do timeout.
Justification:Self-registration is off unless enabled. If it is turned on, add reCAPTCHA to the registration flow and rate-limit the endpoint at the reverse proxy so bulk sign-ups cannot fill the database.

Interaction: User credentials and client registration

157. Weak Access Control for a Resource  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Improper data protection of Keycloak database can allow an attacker to read information not intended for disclosure. Review authorization settings.
Justification:Holds password hashes, OTP secrets (Interaction 1) and each client&#39;s registered redirect URIs. Access is limited to the Keycloak database account and database administrators.

158. Persistent Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Authenticate user' could be a subject to a persistent cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize data store 'Keycloak database' inputs and output.
Justification:Stored values such as client names and user attributes are escaped on output. Login and broker pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat). Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

159. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Authenticate user' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Client display names and user attributes from the database appear on login pages. Login and broker pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat). Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

160. Spoofing of Source Data Store Keycloak database  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Keycloak database may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to incorrect data delivered to Authenticate user. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the source data store.
Justification:Keycloak reaches its database over the configured JDBC connection with a dedicated database account. Restrict that account to the Keycloak schema, require TLS with certificate validation on the JDBC URL (Keycloak does not enforce it), and keep the database on a segment only Keycloak nodes can reach. Shared with Interaction 1.

Interaction: User entries and group memberships

161. Spoofing the Synchronize federated users Process  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Synchronize federated users may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to information disclosure by Active Directory. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination process.
Justification:AD returns entries on the connection Keycloak opened, so a substituted process cannot receive them. With TLS required the connection is encrypted and AD&#39;s certificate is checked.

162. Spoofing the Active Directory External Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Active Directory may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Synchronize federated users. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:A spoofed directory could inject users or group memberships. Use an ldaps:// URL or turn on StartTLS. Keycloak accepts a plaintext ldap:// URL without a warning, so our configuration requires TLS. With TLS on, Keycloak checks AD&#39;s certificate against its truststore and always uses strict hostname verification (LDAPUtil).

163. Potential Lack of Input Validation for Synchronize federated users  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:Data flowing across User entries and group memberships may be tampered with by an attacker. This may lead to a denial of service attack against Synchronize federated users or an elevation of privilege attack against Synchronize federated users or an information disclosure by Synchronize federated users. Failure to verify that input is as expected is a root cause of a very large number of exploitable issues. Consider all paths and the way they handle data. Verify that all input is verified for correctness using an approved list input validation approach.
Justification:Only the attributes the configured mappers read are imported; everything else is ignored. Results are paged in batches of 1,000 by default.

164. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Synchronize federated users' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Imported names and attributes appear on login and account pages and in the Admin Console. Login and account pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat), and the Account and Admin Consoles are React apps that escape rendered values. Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

165. Potential Data Repudiation by Synchronize federated users  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Synchronize federated users claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:Gap: scheduled syncs only write debug logs, and LDAP mappers call user.grantRole with only a debug log line, so nothing records which AD group granted which role. Syncs started from the Admin Console emit an admin event only when Save admin events is on.

166. Data Flow Sniffing  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Data flowing across User entries and group memberships may be sniffed by an attacker. Depending on what type of data an attacker can read, it may be used to attack other parts of the system or simply be a disclosure of information leading to compliance violations. Consider encrypting the data flow.
Justification:Use an ldaps:// URL or turn on StartTLS. Keycloak accepts a plaintext ldap:// URL without a warning, so our configuration requires TLS. With TLS on, Keycloak checks AD&#39;s certificate against its truststore and always uses strict hostname verification (LDAPUtil). Without TLS, directory data and group memberships cross the network in clear text.

167. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Synchronize federated users  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Synchronize federated users crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:Pagination is on by default (batches of 1,000) and a cluster lock stops two syncs of the same provider running at once. Gap: syncs started from the Admin Console skip the minimum-interval check, and no cap on values per attribute was found in the LDAP provider. Needs testing with large groups.

168. Data Flow User entries and group memberships Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:An interrupted sync is retried at the next interval; users already imported stay in place.

169. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Synchronize federated users may be able to impersonate the context of Active Directory in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:Gap: the role mapper matches AD group names to Keycloak role names and creates the role if it doesn&#39;t exist, with no admin-role check like the one 26.8.0 added for identity provider mappers. Anyone who can create a correctly named group under the Roles DN gets that role. Restrict who can create groups under the mapped DN in AD and map only to non-privileged roles.

170. Synchronize federated users May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Active Directory may be able to remotely execute code for Synchronize federated users.
Justification:The process parses requests and directory responses with standard libraries and never evaluates input as code. Keep Keycloak and its Java runtime patched and run it as an unprivileged user.

171. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Synchronize federated users  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Synchronize federated users in order to change the flow of program execution within Synchronize federated users to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:Sync applies directory data only through the mappers configured on the provider; it cannot change which mappers run or what they map to.

Interaction: User profile and policies

172. Spoofing of Source Data Store Keycloak database  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Keycloak database may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to incorrect data delivered to Manage user account (register, reset password, update). Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the source data store.
Justification:Keycloak reaches its database over the configured JDBC connection with a dedicated database account. Restrict that account to the Keycloak schema, require TLS with certificate validation on the JDBC URL (Keycloak does not enforce it), and keep the database on a segment only Keycloak nodes can reach.

173. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Manage user account (register, reset password, update)' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Profile attributes shown on login and account pages are escaped. Login and account pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat), and the Account and Admin Consoles are React apps that escape rendered values. Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

174. Persistent Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Manage user account (register, reset password, update)' could be a subject to a persistent cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize data store 'Keycloak database' inputs and output.
Justification:The default user profile applies validators that reject unsafe characters in names and usernames, and stored values are escaped when rendered. Login and account pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat), and the Account and Admin Consoles are React apps that escape rendered values. Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

175. Weak Access Control for a Resource  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Improper data protection of Keycloak database can allow an attacker to read information not intended for disclosure. Review authorization settings.
Justification:The user profile configuration controls which attributes a user can view or edit, so admin-only attributes stay read-only. Password hashes never leave the credential store, and listing credentials blanks their secret data.

Interaction: User, role, client and flow changes

176. Spoofing of Destination Data Store Keycloak database  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Keycloak database may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being written to the attacker's target instead of Keycloak database. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination data store.
Justification:Keycloak reaches its database over the configured JDBC connection with a dedicated database account. Restrict that account to the Keycloak schema, require TLS with certificate validation on the JDBC URL (Keycloak does not enforce it), and keep the database on a segment only Keycloak nodes can reach.

177. Potential SQL Injection Vulnerability for Keycloak database  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. Any procedure that constructs SQL statements should be reviewed for injection vulnerabilities because SQL Server will execute all syntactically valid queries that it receives. Even parameterized data can be manipulated by a skilled and determined attacker.
Justification:Keycloak writes through JPA/Hibernate with bound parameters, so request and directory values are stored as data, not SQL.

178. Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Administer realm (Admin console) or Keycloak database  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Does Administer realm (Admin console) or Keycloak database take explicit steps to control resource consumption? Resource consumption attacks can be hard to deal with, and there are times that it makes sense to let the OS do the job. Be careful that your resource requests don't deadlock, and that they do timeout.
Justification:Only authenticated admins reach this flow, and each change is a bounded write. Limit admin roles and keep /admin/ on the admin network.

Interaction: Username and password submission

179. Cross Site Request Forgery  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Cross-site request forgery (CSRF or XSRF) is a type of attack in which an attacker forces a user's browser to make a forged request to a vulnerable site by exploiting an existing trust relationship between the browser and the vulnerable web site. In a simple scenario, a user is logged in to web site A using a cookie as a credential. The other browses to web site B. Web site B returns a page with a hidden form that posts to web site A. Since the browser will carry the user's cookie to web site A, web site B now can take any action on web site A, for example, adding an admin to an account. The attack can be used to exploit any requests that the browser automatically authenticates, e.g. by session cookie, integrated authentication, IP whitelisting. The attack can be carried out in many ways such as by luring the victim to a site under control of the attacker, getting the user to click a link in a phishing email, or hacking a reputable web site that the victim will visit. The issue can only be resolved on the server side by requiring that all authenticated state-changing requests include an additional piece of secret payload (canary or CSRF token) which is known only to the legitimate web site and the browser and which is protected in transit through SSL/TLS. See the Forgery Protection property on the flow stencil for a list of mitigations.
Justification:The username and password submission flow could be targeted by forged browser requests. Keycloak includes protections for authentication requests, but the specific flow configuration, request validation, and CSRF protections have not been verified in this threat model. Further testing is needed before marking this threat as mitigated.

180. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Authenticate user  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Authenticate user in order to change the flow of program execution within Authenticate user to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:The Authenticate user process handles username and password submissions from an external browser. Keycloak provides authentication controls, but further review of input handling, custom authentication extensions, and security testing is needed to determine whether malicious input could alter the intended authentication flow or bypass required verification steps.

181. Authenticate user May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:End user (browser) may be able to remotely execute code for Authenticate user.
Justification:The Authenticate user process receives input from an external browser. Although Keycloak processes authentication requests, further review of input validation, authentication components, and relevant security patches is needed to determine whether malicious input could lead to remote code execution.

182. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Authenticate user may be able to impersonate the context of End user (browser) in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:The authentication process handles credentials submitted by an external user. Keycloak must validate credentials and enforce authentication requirements before establishing an authenticated session. Additional verification is needed to confirm that impersonation cannot bypass these controls.

183. Data Flow Username and password submission Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:An attacker or network disruption could interrupt the transmission of authentication credentials between the browser and Keycloak. Further verification is needed to confirm that TLS, connection timeout handling, and availability protections are properly configured.

184. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Authenticate user  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Authenticate user crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:Repeated or malformed authentication requests could affect the availability of the Authenticate user process. Further investigation is needed to verify that rate limiting, resource monitoring, and availability controls are configured to prevent or reduce service disruption.

185. Potential Data Repudiation by Authenticate user  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Authenticate user claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:Keycloak supports authentication event logging, but additional verification is needed to confirm that successful and failed login attempts are recorded, retained, and protected against unauthorized modification. These records are necessary to investigate disputed authentication activities.

186. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Authenticate user' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:The username and password submission is processed by Keycloak, but malicious input could potentially exploit unsafe rendering in authentication pages or custom themes. Further verification of input handling, output encoding, and custom authentication components is needed to confirm protection against cross-site scripting.

187. Spoofing the End user (browser) External Entity  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:End user (browser) may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Authenticate user. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:The username and password submission flow originates from an external browser that could be impersonated by an attacker. Keycloak validates submitted credentials before establishing an authenticated session, but further verification of session management, brute-force protection, and authentication controls is needed to determine whether browser impersonation risks are adequately mitigated.

Interaction: Validated user and federated roles

188. Synchronize federated users Process Memory Tampered  [State: Not Applicable]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:If Synchronize federated users is given access to memory, such as shared memory or pointers, or is given the ability to control what Authenticate user executes (for example, passing back a function pointer.), then Synchronize federated users can tamper with Authenticate user. Consider if the function could work with less access to memory, such as passing data rather than pointers. Copy in data provided, and then validate it.
Justification:Both ends are parts of the same Keycloak server process; the data is passed as an in-memory object, not across a trust boundary or shared memory.

189. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Authenticate user' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Federated attributes shown on the update-profile page are escaped. Login and account pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat), and the Account and Admin Consoles are React apps that escape rendered values. Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

190. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Authenticate user may be able to impersonate the context of Synchronize federated users in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:The roles handed to Authenticate user come from AD group memberships through the role and group mappers. Gap: the role mapper matches AD group names to Keycloak role names and creates the role if it doesn&#39;t exist, with no admin-role check like the one 26.8.0 added for identity provider mappers. Anyone who can create a correctly named group under the Roles DN gets that role. Restrict who can create groups under the mapped DN in AD and map only to non-privileged roles.

191. Spoofing of the Email service External Destination Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Email service may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being sent to the attacker's target instead of Email service. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:Configure the realm&#39;s SMTP server with SSL or StartTLS and authentication. Keycloak 26.8.1 fixed CVE-2026-107121, where starttls=true still allowed a plaintext downgrade, so run 26.8.1 or later.

192. External Entity Email service Potentially Denies Receiving Data  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Email service claims that it did not receive data from a process on the other side of the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:SEND_RESET_PASSWORD and SEND_VERIFY_EMAIL events record that Keycloak sent the email when Save events is on (off by default, turned on by our configuration). The mail server&#39;s logs cover delivery.

193. Data Flow Verification and reset emails Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:If the email doesn&#39;t arrive, the user requests a new one; the unused action token expires.
